Some people have dysfunctional families man.
A couple of years back, I started smashing this short, pretty chick I met at the gym. What impressed me the most was how much of a hustler she was... That girl used to grind. Came to find out that the moment she finished high school at 17, she immediately became the sole* breadwinner of the family. And mark you, she had both a dad and a mom (both healthy, no disabilities), not to mention they all lived under one roof. So it wasn't like they were some estranged family. Her bum ass dad would literally chill indoors all day with their mom waiting for their 17 year old daughter to bring home the bread in the evening. She got so burnt out after a year of working daily to support the family that she crashed, and had to take 3 months off just to stabilise.
I remember lying in bed one day with her and she insisted on showing me a text her mom had sent her. She'd sent her around 10k, but apparently that wasn't enough. The gaslighting and passive aggressive speak was disgusting. It's insane to speak to anyone like that, let alone your kid, and especially so after they've just sent you money they could've used for themselves.
Made me appreciate my own family, even though we have our own flaws and what not (as all families do)

The crime is absolutely barbaric, and it wiped the wifes history who was a star in her own right as she is now not discussed in wrestling halls, case in point that I can no longer remember her name. But we need to have a serious discussion not just on TBIs but colleagues duty to report.
Regals statement on Raw during Benoits life celebration has one of the most eerie silences in it with hindsight. It is truly horrfying to think whilst so many were celebrating him, there were people already just wondering.
Of course this could tie into the theory that the true details were beginning to leak during the episode, however that is speculation and conjecture at absolute best, I'm unaware of any statement confirming that.
I was actually downloading the episode unaware of the details, on Limewire, when it started to go widespread. To see the peers and seeds shutting down in real time unaware that it was the internet quietly and collectively washing it hands of Chris Benoit, feels like a little piece of history. In the end, when I woke up the next day, the episode was locked at just over 50%, with myself as the only person. I mused on how odd it was, got myself a cuppa, and looked at the news.
Then I too, clicked remove and delete, washing my hands of Chris Benoit.
